title: Application Security Engineer
description: Embed security into every stage of the software development lifecycle (DevSecOps), conduct secure code reviews, and automate SAST/DAST/SCA tooling.

goal.objective: Empower software developers to write secure code by default, embedding automated security gates and threat modeling into modern CI/CD pipelines.

learn.summary: Master STRIDE threat modeling, manual secure code review, SAST (Semgrep, SonarQube), DAST (ZAP), Software Composition Analysis (Snyk/Trivy), and DevSecOps pipelines.
key_competencies: Secure Code Review (TypeScript, Python, Java, Go)
Software Supply Chain Security & SBOM Generation

capstone_projects.title: Automated DevSecOps CI/CD Security Pipeline
capstone_projects.description: Build an automated security gate in GitHub Actions integrating Semgrep SAST, Trivy container scanning, Sigstore cryptographic artifact signing, and SARIF triage.

capstone_projects.title: Cloud-Native Web Application Firewall & Micro-Proxy
capstone_projects.description: Architect a high-performance WAF reverse proxy enforcing OWASP Core Rule Set, automated bot mitigation, and distributed IP reputation scoring.

interview_focus: OWASP Top 10 Root Causes & Defenses (SQLi, SSRF, XSS, IDOR, Broken Object Level Auth)
OAuth2.0 / OIDC Grant Flows, PKCE Mechanics & JWT Vulnerabilities (Alg=None, Key Confusion)
Software Supply Chain Security (SLSA Framework, SBOM Generation, CycloneDX, Sigstore)
Content Security Policy (CSP Level 3), CORS Headers & Subresource Integrity (SRI)
Threat Modeling Methodologies (STRIDE, DREAD, Attack Trees) for Cloud Microservices

tree.name: Foundations of Application Security
tree.description: Establish an uncompromised Application Security foundation: master web application architecture, secure software development lifecycles (SSDLC), and security engineering principles.

resources.title: What is AppSec and Why it's Important
Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner

children.name: Essential Cybersecurity & Information Security Concepts
children.description: Master information security core principles: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability (CIA Triad), Defense-in-Depth, Principle of Least Privilege, Separation of Duties, Fail-Safe Defaults, and minimizing attack surfaces.

resources.title: Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner

children.name: Web & API Application Architecture Fundamentals
children.description: Understand web application internals from an attacker and defender perspective: HTTP/HTTPS protocol mechanics, request/response headers, cookie security flags (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`), RESTful APIs, GraphQL AST query parsing, and WebSockets.

resources.title: How The Web Works: A Primer for Newcomers to Web Development
REST API Crash Course - Learn the basics of RESTful API Development

children.name: Networking & Operating System Basics for AppSec
children.description: Master underlying OS and networking security: TCP/IP stack vulnerabilities, TLS 1.3 handshake and cipher suite negotiation, DNS resolution attacks (cache poisoning, rebinding), Linux user namespaces, and file permissions.

children.name: Secure Software Development Life Cycle (SSDLC)
children.description: Implement Secure Software Development Lifecycles (SSDLC): integrating security into Agile/DevOps workflows (BSIMM, OWASP SAMM), security gates, and shifting security left from design to production.

resources.title: OWASP SAMM: Software Assurance Maturity Model
Secure SDLC - What is Secure SDLC? Software Development Lifecycle
Secure SDLC: Integrating Security into Your Development Pipeline

children.name: The Application Security Engineer Role & Collaboration
children.description: Define the modern AppSec Engineer role: partnering with product and engineering teams, threat modeling, automating security guardrails, and fostering a security champions network.

resources.title: What Does an AppSec Engineer Do?
Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner
Application Security Engineer Explained - What Is AppSec & How To Become One

tree.name: Core Secure Design & Implementation Skills
tree.description: Master core application security disciplines: threat modeling, defensive coding, identity architecture, cryptography, and software supply chain security.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 Web Application Security Risks
Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner
Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner

children.name: Threat Modeling & Secure Design Principles
children.description: Master architectural threat modeling: STRIDE methodology (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege), constructing Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs), defining trust boundaries, attack trees, and risk scoring with DREAD.

resources.title: Threat Modeling: Identifying Threats with STRIDE

children.name: Secure Coding Best Practices & Defensive Programming
children.description: Implement secure coding across stacks: defending against the OWASP Top 10: parameterized queries to eliminate SQL injection, context-aware output encoding to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), anti-CSRF token synchronization, and safe deserialization.

resources.title: OWASP Secure Coding Practices Cheat Sheet
Secure Coding Best Practices - How to Write Safe Code
Introduction to Application Security - The Most Important Security Concepts Explained

children.name: Authentication, Authorization & Session Management
children.description: Architect enterprise authentication and authorization: OAuth 2.0 and OIDC flows, eliminating Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR), cryptographically secure session generation, preventing JWT signature bypass attacks (`none` algorithm, key confusion), and WebAuthn/Passkeys.

resources.title: Authentication Basics: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
API Authentication EXPLAINED! 🔐 OAuth vs JWT vs API Keys 🚀

children.name: Applied Cryptography for Secure Systems
children.description: Apply cryptographic standards correctly: modern password hashing (Argon2id, bcrypt), symmetric authenticated encryption (AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305), asymmetric digital signatures (Ed25519, RSA-4096), secure random number generation (`crypto.randomBytes`), and eliminating hardcoded keys.

children.name: Input Validation, Sanitization & Output Encoding
children.description: Enforce strict input validation and output encoding: schema-based validation (Zod, Pydantic), eliminating Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) by restricting internal IP ranges (IMDSv2, 169.254.169.254), and configuring Content Security Policy (CSP Level 3 with nonces).

resources.title: Basics of SQL Injection - Penetration Testing for Ethical Hackers

children.name: Secrets Management & Secure Configuration
children.description: Master secrets lifecycle management: scanning repositories with TruffleHog / GitGuardian, centralizing secrets in HashiCorp Vault or cloud secret managers, dynamic secret leasing, and eliminating plaintext secrets from source code and container layers.

resources.title: OWASP Secure Configuration Management Cheat Sheet
What is HashiCorp Vault? | Vault Explained
AWS Secrets Manager Explained | Protecting your secrets on AWS

children.name: Data Security & Privacy Principles
children.description: Protect data at rest and in transit: column-level encryption, tokenization of financial/PII data, data masking, and complying with privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA).

resources.title: Data Encryption Standard (DES) vs. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)
GDPR Explained: A Guide to the General Data Protection Regulation
Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner

children.name: Software Composition Analysis (SCA) & Dependency Management
children.description: Manage third-party open-source risk: Software Composition Analysis (SCA), Software Bill of Materials (SBOM in SPDX/CycloneDX formats), vulnerability scanning with Snyk / Grype, and preventing dependency confusion attacks.

resources.title: What is Software Composition Analysis (SCA)? Explained Visually
